audit_scope.description: This batch covers: wallet batched calls API (EIP-5792), Muir Glacier fork difficulty calculation, Byzantium fork activation (EIP-609), EIP governance process (EIP-1), and empty account prohibition (EIP-7523). EIP-1 and EIP-5792 are not EL-internal protocol specs but define interfaces and processes relevant to the ecosystem.

misclassified_entities.reason: From EIP-5792: 'Ethereum Blockchain' is the system itself, not an external entity. The blockchain is the target being analyzed, not an external actor crossing a trust boundary.
From Muir Glacier: 'Block Processor' is an internal node component that processes blocks for chain updates. It is part of the EL node, not an external entity.
From EIP-1: 'EIP Author' is a participant in the governance process. EIP-1 is a meta/process EIP, not a protocol specification. Authors do not interact with the EL at runtime.
From EIP-1: 'EIP Editor' is a governance role. Editors do not interact with the EL at runtime; they manage the EIP repository.
From EIP-1: 'Ethereum Core Developers' is a governance body. They make protocol decisions but do not represent a runtime external entity interacting with the EL.

trusted_external_entities.name: dApp via Wallet JSON-RPC (wallet_sendCalls)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-5792: dApps submit batched call requests to wallets via JSON-RPC. The dApp is an untrusted web application that may submit malicious call batches, attempt fingerprinting via capability queries, or request excessive permissions. All requests must be validated and user-approved.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet User (Human Approver)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-5792: the human user approves or rejects batched transaction requests. While the user controls the wallet, they may be socially engineered or deceived by malicious dApps. The wallet must present clear information for informed consent.

trusted_external_entities.name: Fingerprinting Attacker via wallet_getCapabilities
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-5792: attackers may use capability queries to fingerprint wallet implementations. Wallets should consider privacy implications of capability responses and may need to limit or normalize responses.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via devp2p (Muir Glacier Blocks)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From Muir Glacier and EIP-609: peers broadcast blocks over unauthenticated P2P. Block headers must have difficulty independently validated using the correct fork rules (9M offset for Muir Glacier, Byzantium EIPs for post-fork blocks). Non-upgraded peers will be rejected.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: wallet_sendCalls JSON-RPC -> Wallet Validation -> Transaction Construction -> eth_sendRawTransaction
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Wallet must validate request schema, chainId support, capability requirements, and duplicate IDs. Batch identifiers must be unpredictable (CSPRNG). User must explicitly approve each batch. Atomicity guarantees depend on wallet capability.

Wallet must present all call details clearly to the user. User approval is the final gate before transaction submission. Social engineering attacks on users are out of scope for protocol-level mitigation but wallet UX should minimize confusion.

Capability responses may leak wallet implementation details. Wallets should consider normalizing responses across implementations to reduce fingerprinting surface. No sensitive state should be exposed through capability queries.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: devp2p block import -> Fork-Aware Header Validation -> Difficulty Recalculation
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Blocks must be validated against the correct fork rules based on block number. Muir Glacier blocks use 9M offset for difficulty bomb. Byzantium blocks must enable all constituent EIPs atomically. Peers on old forks will be disconnected.
